description: The application reads the cache, loads from the database on a miss and stores the result with a TTL.
Each write updates the cache and the database before it is acknowledged: fresh reads, slower writes.
Writes are acknowledged from the cache and flushed to the database later; fast, but unflushed writes are lost if the cache fails.
Writes go only to the database and the cache fills on read, which keeps write-once data out of the cache.
Eviction by least recent access (adapts fast, hurt by scans) or by least frequent access (keeps long-lived popular keys).
Many concurrent misses on one expired hot key, all sending the same expensive query to the database.
Concurrent misses for a key share the first miss's in-flight load, so the database sees one query.
A random extra amount added to each TTL so entries written together do not expire together.
